title: Mills office, pay on the road, and the Cotton Club as home base
summary: Pay came from the road manager, and the band always returned to the Cotton Club between tours.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: No. That's a great shame isn't it. A great pity. Well, let's see then, Cootie, you left -- I think the band left the Cotton Club, maybe in '31 or something, and started going out on the road. Well, let's see. They were being handled by Irving Mills, and it was with the Mills office. You used to get your paychecks every week through the Mills office, didn't you? Or did Duke pay off?
We'd usually get paid off on the road.
Whoever the road manager was that day.
But we always came back to the Cotton Club, though.
Yeah. We never did leave for good.
They'd have a band in there. Maybe whoever was in there would just work until we got out of our thing and came back.
And then you came back and did a new show.
Yeah. We'd come back all the time.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, that was good, because it meant that you had a home base.
